\section{Results: Quality}
\label{sec:results-quality}

This section reports the quality axis of the study on the single-hop
parity benchmarks in scope for this preprint (C1): how much
cross-document attention can be removed before answer quality drops
below the parity band.

\subsection{Train-free mask sweep}
\label{sec:results-quality-sweep}

The primary quality result is the train-free sweep: for every combination
of primary model, base/instruct variant, dataset, and mask variant, the
mask is swapped at inference on stock weights and evaluated with $\geq 3$
seeds. If the median gap to \texttt{full} is smaller than the
non-inferiority margin $\Delta$ (Section~\ref{sec:method-delta}) the
train-free result supports the parity claim for that cell.

Table~\ref{tab:t2} reports train-free quality on the parity-detection
datasets.

\subsection{Finetuned quality}
\label{sec:results-quality-finetune}

The train-free sweep shows a quality gap between \texttt{ddi\_qf} and
\texttt{full} (Table~\ref{tab:t2}): on hotpot\_qa, EM drops from 0.57
(full) to 0.31 (ddi\_qf). We close this gap via self-distillation: the
student model runs under \texttt{ddi\_qf} and is trained to match the
teacher's answer-position logits under \texttt{full}, using KL divergence
on the answer tokens. Only the top 8 of 28 decoder layers are trainable
(1.86B parameters); the rest are frozen.

Table~\ref{tab:t4} reports the finetuned quality on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct.
After sequential finetuning (13.5 GPU-hours, 26{,}231 steps), ddi\_qf
matches full on hotpot\_qa (0.46 = 0.46 EM). Mixed-layout finetuning
(13.8 GPU-hours, coin-flip per record between sequential and restart
positions) maintains parity at a slightly lower level (0.39 vs 0.40).
Restart-only finetuning (13.8 GPU-hours, restart positions exclusively)
also achieves parity (0.42 vs 0.39). The full-quality regression
(0.57$\to$0.46$\to$0.40$\to$0.39) is a known trade-off:
the finetune shifts capacity from full-causal to block-diagonal attention.

On musique, the 8-layer finetune leaves a residual gap (0.13 vs 0.23 EM,
$\Delta$=+0.10). Doubling the trainable layers to 16 (3.73B params,
17.97 GPU-hours, building on the 8L checkpoint) narrows the musique gap
to $\Delta$=+0.04 (0.19 vs 0.23 EM) while maintaining hotpot parity
(Table~\ref{tab:t4-16l}). The student perplexity (1.453) nearly matches
the teacher (1.446), and the remaining musique gap is at the resolution
limit of a 100-record eval.

The restart-quality result is reported separately
(Table~\ref{tab:t4_restart}): despite closing the perplexity gap under
restart-only training (restart 1.629 $<$ sequential 1.638), the generation
gap under restart positions persists across all three finetuning strategies
(0.07 vs 0.42 EM on hotpot\_qa). See
Section~\ref{sec:limitations} for the full discussion.

\subsection{Closure across document counts}
\label{sec:results-quality-docsweep}

Phase~1 established that the mask quality gap on the \emph{base} model grows
with document count (Section~\ref{sec:results-quality-sweep}). Phase~3 tests
whether the finetuned closure survives at higher document counts --- the
operating point DDI is designed for. Table~\ref{tab:t5} reports the tuned
checkpoint (sequential finetune, 8 trainable layers) at $N \in \{2, 5, 10\}$
documents on hotpot\_qa.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering\small
\caption{T5 --- quality vs document count on the tuned checkpoint, hotpot\_qa,
    100 records per cell. The gap \emph{closes} at $N{=}10$, the opposite of
    the base-model pattern in Phase~1.}
\label{tab:t5}
\IfFileExists{generated/T5.tex}{%
    \input{generated/T5.tex}%
}{%
    \todoreport{T5 document-count sweep}{run phase3 sweep}%
}
\end{table}

The gap does not grow with $N$; it shrinks. At $N{=}10$ the EM gap is zero
(0.46 vs 0.46), and the F1 gap narrows to 0.03. This is the opposite of the
base-model pattern (Phase~1), where the gap widened with document count. The
finetune taught the model to work \emph{under the mask}, not merely the task
--- a closure that generalizes to the document counts where DDI's compute and
caching benefits are largest.
